attributes.title: RIPA Stop Data

body.value:
What is required? Assembly Bill 953 (AB 953) requires each state and local agency in California that employs peace officers to annually report to the Attorney General data on all stops conducted by the agency's peace officers. This includes the California Highway Patrol, a city or county law enforcement agency, and California state or university educational institutions, but does not include probation officers and officers in a custodial setting.

A “stop” is defined in Government Code section 12525.5(g)(2), with further information and scenarios detailed in the implementing regulations. The bill requires officers to collect specific information on each stop, including elements of the stop circumstances and the perceived identity characteristics of the individual(s) stopped. For additional information, you may want to explore the RIPA Regulations and Laws page.

What is the AB 953 timeline? Law enforcement agencies began collecting and submitting this data on a rolling basis according to the number of sworn peace officers they employ. The eight largest agencies in the state (those employing 1,000+) peace officers began collecting the data as of July 1, 2018. Since then, additional agencies have started collecting data on their stops in each successive calendar year. All agencies are required to start collecting data for AB 953 as of January 1, 2022.

Data available on OpenJustice: Files are available to download for the time period of 7/1/2018 – 12/31/2024. Analyses of RIPA data are presented in the RIPA Advisory Board’s Annual Report. Tables summarizing agency-level data are published in the Statutorily Mandated Tables.xlsx, with accompanying descriptions in the Statutorily Mandated Tables - Read Me.pdf.

body.value: California law requires any government entity that executes a warrant, or obtains information in an emergency from an electronic communication service provider or from an electronic device shall notify the identified targets of the warrant or emergency request that information about them has been compelled or obtained. The law requires that the government entity provide specific information about the investigation under which the information is sought and provide a copy of the warrant or a written statement setting forth facts giving rise to the emergency. (California Penal Code s. 1546.2)

attributes.title: Crime Gun and Firearms Dealer Inspection Data

body.value:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) publishes information on firearms that were used in a crime, suspected of being used in a crime, or illegally possessed and reported to the Automated Firearms System (AFS) by California Law Enforcement Agencies under Assembly Bill (AB) 1191 that came into effect in 2021. DOJ also publishes information on inspections of California firearms dealers under Senate Bill (SB) 965 that came into effect in 2024.

The Crime Gun Appendix data contains the corresponding appendix data for the AB 1191 crime gun report, including firearms tracing data on the source dealers associated with crime guns recovered in California, county and city level breakdowns of crime guns, as well as manufacturers associated with crime guns recovered in California.

The Dealer Inspection Appendix data contains data on the results of DOJ's inspections of firearms dealers, including violations associated with the inspected dealers, background checks submitted by firearm and ammunition dealers, as well as crime guns and stolen firearms associated with insepcted dealers.

attributes.title: Violent Crimes Committed Against Senior Citizens

body.value: Violent Crimes Committed Against Senior Citizens (VCASC) data are collected from various LEAs throughout the state on a monthly basis. The data set provides summary statistical data on the total number persons 60 years of age or older who were victims of homicide, rape, robbery, or aggravated assault.

body.value: Anti-Reproductive Rights Crimes (ARRC) is reported by various law enforcement agencies (LEA) throughout the State, on a monthly basis. The data set contains information on crimes that are committed against reproductive health services providers, clients, assistants or the facilities where these services are provided or at a place of worship because of the church's beliefs regarding reproductive rights and includes the location of the crime, victim type (individual/property), race/ethnicity, gender of victims and suspects, weapon involved, and property loss or damage.

This dataset includes aggregated counts of arrests by county, gender, race/ethnic group, age group, and offense level.

attributes.title: Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Personnel

body.value: California LEAs report counts of the number of full-time sworn and non-sworn, male and female law enforcement personnel (LEP) employed. The DOJ also collects the number of attorneys, investigators, and clerical and other criminal justice personnel (CJP) employed by district attorneys and public defenders; and probation officers and other staff employed by probation departments. The DOJ collects the Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Personnel (LECJP) data through one-day surveys of each reporting year: criminal justice personnel counts are taken on June 30th and law enforcement personnel counts are taken on October 31st.

body.value: State and local law enforcement agencies that employ peace officers provide Civilians' Complaints Against Peace Officers (CCAPO) data via an annual summary. The information includes the number of criminal and non-criminal complaints reported by civilians and the number of complaints sustained. Assembly Bill 953 (2015) modified the reporting requirements to expand the types of findings and also include complaints based upon racial and identity profiling claims. 2016 was the first year of collection under the new reporting requirements.

attributes.title: Law Enforcement Officers Killed or Assaulted

body.value: Law Enforcement Officers Killed or Assaulted (LEOKA) data are reported as part of the Federal Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program by LEAs throughout the state. LEOKA data are summary data, meaning it is a collection of information describing the totality of incidents, not a collection at the detailed, incident level. LEOKA is a federally mandated collection. From the 1960's until 1990, the CJSC did not retain any of the LEOKA data; the forms were passed along to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). In 1990, the DOJ began to collect and retain the data from the LEOKA form for statistical purposes, but it wasn't until 2000, that full retention at the State level was defined and standardized.

body.value: Crimes and Clearances are reported monthly by LEAs throughout the state. The data is reported as part of the Federal Bureau of Investigation's (FBI), Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program and includes the number of actual offenses as well as the number of clearances as per the UCR guidelines. Supplemental data are also collected on the nature of some of the crime types and the value of property stolen and recovered. The information is used to provide statistical data on the offenses of: criminal homicide, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft, and arson.

The JCPSS includes basic demographic information of the juvenile referred and the juvenile probation or court disposition (the system does not track individuals through the system).

body.value: State and local law enforcement agencies and correctional facilities report information on deaths that occur in custody or during the process of arrest in compliance with Section 12525 of the California Government Code. Contributors include: California law enforcement agencies, county probation departments, state hospitals, and state correctional facilities. Data are subject to revision as reports are received by the California Department of Justice (DOJ); figures in previous and current releases may not match.

attributes.title: Domestic Violence Related Calls for Assistance

body.value: Domestic Violence-Related Calls for Assistance (DVRCA) are reported by various LEAs throughout the State on a monthly basis. The DVRCA data set provides summary statistical data on the total number of domestic violence related calls for assistance received by the LEAs, the number of cases involving weapons, and the type of weapon used during the reported incident.

body.value: The Hate Crime Prosecution Survey data are submitted annually by district attorneys and elected city attorneys. Hate crime acts involve the intent to cause physical injury, emotional suffering, or property damage where there is a reasonable cause to believe that the crime was motivated by the victim's race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or physical or mental disability. Hate Crime Prosecution data includes the number of hate crime cases referred to prosecutors, the number of cases filed in court, and the outcome of the cases reaching a disposition in the report year.

body.value: The Use of Force Incident Reporting incidents that result in serious bodily injury or death or involved the discharge of a firearm are reported annually from LEAs and other entities throughout the state that employ peace officers. The Use of Force Incident Reporting data is narrowly defined and does not represent the totality of use of force incidents that occur in California. LEAs are only required to report use of force incidents that result in serious bodily injury or death of either the civilian or the officer and all incidents where there is a discharge of a firearm. As such, caution must be used when using the data for comparisons or in calculating rates.

body.value: Publishing of Automatic Record Relief (ARR) Annual Statistics was mandated by Assembly Bill (AB) 1076 (Chapter 578, Statutes of 2019). The ARR program reviews statewide criminal justice databases and provides record relief for eligible arrests and convictions automatically without the need for individuals to submit a petition. AB 1076 required the California Department of Justice to annually publish on the OpenJustice Web portal, as described under Penal Code section 13010, statistics for each county regarding the total number of arrests granted relief pursuant to Section 851.93 of the California Penal Code, the total number of convictions granted relief pursuant to Section 1203.425 of the California Penal Code, the total number of convictions prohibited from automatic relief pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 1203.425 of the California Penal Code, and the percentage of arrests for which the state summary criminal history information does not include a disposition.

attributes.title: Arrests Related to Firearms Without a Serial Number

body.value: Publishing annual statistics on arrests made by law enforcement agencies for offenses related to firearms without a valid state or federal serial number was mandated by Assembly Bill (AB) 97 (Chapter 223, Statutes of 2023). AB 97 required the California Department of Justice to annually publish on the OpenJustice Web portal, as described under Penal Code section 13010.

body.value:
The Department of Justice (DOJ) collects information on gun violence restraining orders (GVRO). Courts and law enforcement utilize the California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System (CLETS) to enter the data into the California Restraining and Protective Order System (CARPOS). The collection of these data began on January 1, 2016 when Assembly Bill (AB) 1014 came into effect. At the time, only immediate family members and officers could petition the court for a GVRO against persons who pose a threat to themselves or others. Through AB 61, the legislature expanded the list individuals who could petition the court for a GVRO to include an employer, a coworker, or an employee or teacher of a secondary or postsecondary school; this bill came into effect September 1, 2020.

The GVRO ReadMe (Counts) and data file - The counts in the dataset reflect what is in CARPOS at the time of data extraction. The data include the of the number of GVROs issued by type, county, and year.
